record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Let S-Topd be the full category of strong d-spaces with continuous mappings. Is S-Topd reflective in Top0, the category of T0 spaces and continuous mappings?

evidence.quote: Question 8.12. Is S-Topd reflective in Top0 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:

(a) A topological space is called T_0 if for any two distinct points there is an open set containing exactly one of them. On any T_0 space X, the specialization order is defined by x ≤ y iff x ∈ cl({y}). Throughout, every space considered is T_0 and is regarded as a poset via this order.

(b) A nonempty subset D of a poset is directed if every two elements of D have an upper bound in D. A T_0 space X is called a d-space (or monotone convergence space) if its specialization order is a directed-complete partial order (dcpo) and every directed subset D ⊆ X has its supremum ⋁D as a limit point of D in X (equivalently, the closure of D contains ⋁D and the principal filter generated by ⋁D is the set of limits of D).

(c) A T_0 space X is called a strong d-space if for every directed subset D ⊆ X, every point x ∈ X with x ≤ ⋁D in the specialization order, and every open neighborhood U of x, there exists d ∈ D such that the principal up-set ↑d intersects U; equivalently, the strong d-space condition strengthens the d-space condition by requiring that suprema of directed sets be reached "uniformly" by open neighborhoods of points below them.

(d) Let Top_0 denote the category whose objects are T_0 topological spaces and whose morphisms are continuous maps. Let S-Top_d denote the full subcategory of Top_0 whose objects are exactly the strong d-spaces.

(e) A full subcategory A of a category B is called reflective if the inclusion functor A ↪ B has a left adjoint; equivalently, for every object X of B there exists an object r(X) of A and a morphism η_X : X → r(X) such that every morphism from X into an object of A factors uniquely through η_X.

Problem: Determine whether S-Top_d is a reflective subcategory of Top_0. That is, decide whether for every T_0 space X there exists a strong d-space r(X) together with a continuous map η_X : X → r(X) such that for every continuous map f : X → Y with Y a strong d-space, there is a unique continuous map f̄ : r(X) → Y with f̄ ∘ η_X = f.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not locate a published resolution to the question of whether the full subcategory of strong d-spaces is reflective in the category of T_0 spaces. Related work on strong well-filtered spaces, R-spaces, and open well-filtered spaces by Shen, Xi, Xu, Zhao and others continues to appear (including a 2025 preprint on strong well-filteredness of upper topology on sup-complete posets), but none of the located sources explicitly settle the reflectivity of S-Top_d in Top_0.

status_evidence.title: Strong well-filteredness of upper topology on sup-complete posets
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces a new class of T_0 spaces (strong R-spaces) stronger than R-spaces and strongly well-filtered spaces; discusses related categorical/topological properties but does not state reflectivity of S-Top_d in Top_0.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study strong variants of d/well-filtered spaces without resolving the reflectivity question.

status_evidence.title: Further studies on open well-filtered spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies open well-filtered spaces and their categorical properties; does not provide a resolution to the reflectivity of strong d-spaces in Top_0.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent literature on well-filtered variants does not settle the question.
